solutions.check: 32 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), agrees with the 30 answers the paper printed

clue.text: A bitter's sent back by certain groups

indicators.note: sent back tells us the whole string, a plus the bitter ones, is read from its end

parts.note: tarts is a plural word for bitter-tasting ones, the 's read as a plural

explanation.surface: A glass of bitter beer is returned by some groups of drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses A TARTS as a whole, giving the layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers of rock or levels of society, so they are certain groups or classes.

clue.text: Youth wanted to skin fish

parts.note: to strip is to peel or skin
the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A young man wanted to gut and skin a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripling is a lad, a young man not yet fully grown.

clue.text: Denying getting engineer to sort out fault

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army's engineering corps

indicators.note: to sort out a muddle means to rearrange it into order

explanation.surface: An engineer refuses the job of fixing a fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sort out' shuffles FAULT into FUTAL. RE (Royal Engineers) is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Refutal is the act of refuting or contradicting, which is denying.

clue.text: Poles pretended to follow craft back — or did

indicators.note: to follow means the poles and the pretending come after the craft
back means the word for craft is turned to read backwards

parts.note: art is skill, or craft
N and S are the north and south poles
acted means pretended

explanation.surface: Polish people put on a show after a boat turned back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses ART to give TRA; 'to follow' places NS ACTED after it. 'Poles' looks like people from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact business is to carry it out, so transacted is did.

clue.text: Produce notes about the choice of water sport

indicators.note: about means one word goes round the other, the singing wrapped around the picking

parts.note: to produce musical notes is to sing
a cull is a selection or choice, as of animals

explanation.surface: Someone produces musical notes about which water sport to pick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CULL inside SING. 'Produce' looks like a noun (fruit and vegetables), but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculling is propelling a boat with oars, a rowing sport on a river.

clue.text: Controlled study can net results

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a tin is a can

indicators.note: results suggests the letters are what comes out of a reworking, a rearranged outcome

explanation.surface: A controlled experiment shows what a fishing net can catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Continent means self-restrained, able to hold back, so controlled.

clue.text: A game bird

explanation.surface: Playing at shooting a gamebird.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of fun or a prank, and also a songbird such as the skylark.

clue.text: Fancy, going around in an imitation!

indicators.note: going around means the imitation word encloses the other piece

parts.note: an image is a copy or likeness

explanation.surface: Something fancy goes around in a copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to suppose or picture it, which is to imagine.

clue.text: Colour, being inexperienced

explanation.surface: A pale face from being new to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is a colour of grass, and a green recruit is a novice, new and untrained.

clue.text: Supported by the church at one time

parts.note: on means resting upon, supported by
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A congregation was supported by the church in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some point in the past.

clue.text: The chorus don't!

explanation.surface: A choir is told to stop singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrain is the repeated chorus of a song, and to refrain is to hold back, so a command to not do something.

clue.text: Managed to return to class and report

indicators.note: to return means the word for managed is turned to read backwards

parts.note: ran a business means managed it
a rate is a class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: Someone managed to go back to class and give a report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses RAN to give NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell a story, to give an account or report.

clue.text: New building is, repeat is, a cake-shop

indicators.note: a new building of the letters means they are put together in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new building is, to repeat, a bakery.
explanation.definitionFit: A patisserie is a French-style bakery selling pastries and cakes.

clue.text: Autograph the writing on the wall?

explanation.surface: A celebrity scrawls their name on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature autograph is a sign of one's name, and the writing on the wall is a warning omen or sign of doom.

clue.text: Bring down the rate

parts.note: reads like cutting a price or interest charge, but means reducing speed

explanation.surface: A bank lowers its lending charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To slow is to reduce one's speed, so to bring down the rate of travel.

clue.text: 49 + 51 — a hundred — it's wrong!

parts.note: 49 in Roman numerals is IL (one before fifty)
51 in Roman numerals is LI, fifty and one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
it, the possessive 's dropped

explanation.surface: A sum is done and the total of a hundred is declared wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: IL for 49 is an informal Roman numeral (strictly XLIX), a crossword liberty; IT comes from 'it's', the 's linking to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means forbidden by law or custom, that is, wrong to do.

clue.text: Claim parking time before work starts

parts.note: a title is a legal claim or right
P stands for parking on road signs
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Asserting a right to park for a while before the working day.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the page with a book's name comes before the work itself starts.
explanation.definitionFit: The page bearing a book's name is printed at the front, ahead of the text.

clue.text: A stiff climb for the first mate and others

parts.note: Eve was Adam's wife in Genesis, the first spouse
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A tough mountain ascent for the first officer and the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first mate' looks nautical; it is Eve, Adam's mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest, the world's highest mountain, is the hardest climb of all.

clue.text: Free test — sales weak

indicators.note: free means the letters are loosed from their order to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A free trial sold poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteless food is bland and insipid, lacking strength of flavour.

clue.text: "Language is called the — of thought." (Carlyle)

parts.note: a quotation with a gap: Thomas Carlyle likened language to the clothing that thought wears

explanation.surface: A gap-fill from a famous saying by Thomas Carlyle, the Victorian essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: In the quotation language dresses thought as clothing dresses a body, so the gap is an item of clothing.

clue.text: The beak making a stand

explanation.surface: A magistrate takes the stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beak' is also British slang for a magistrate, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Rostrum is a zoological term for a bird's bill, and also a raised platform for a speaker.

clue.text: The serving m* needing large flask

parts.note: RM, the Royal Marines, are men serving in the forces
OS is short for outsize, a clothing size meaning large

explanation.surface: Butlers bring a big vacuum flask to a picnic.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed word after 'serving' is smudged; 'men' fits, as RM is the Royal Marines, the British naval infantry. OS (outsize) is a British label for large clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thermos is a vacuum flask, a trade name that became the general word.

clue.text: Tribal doctor given something to eat

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
a bite is a snack, something to eat

explanation.surface: A tribal healer is offered food.
explanation.definitionFit: Moabite means belonging to the ancient people of Moab in the Bible, a tribe or nation.

clue.text: Calculated project

explanation.surface: A plan that has been worked out ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast a horoscope or accounts is to calculate them, and to cast a shadow or a line is to throw or project it.

clue.text: Funny business with pests not finished

parts.note: Co is short for company, a business

indicators.note: not finished means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: mice are household pests

explanation.surface: A company's dealings with vermin left half done are laughable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' drops the E from MICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic means amusing or laughable.

clue.text: May be meaner, true, yet offer some payment

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: An employer may be meaner but still pays a little.
explanation.definitionFit: To remunerate is to pay someone for work or service.

clue.text: Person exercising requires some house-room

indicators.note: some means only part of the hyphenated phrase supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Someone working out needs a bit of space at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercising' means making use of something, as one exercises a right.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is one who employs or makes use of something, so exercising it.

clue.text: A French party which has to be open

parts.note: un is the French for a
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A French party where everything must be left open.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or parcel is to open it.

clue.text: Edge back accompanied by a heroine

indicators.note: back tells us the word for edge is read from its end

parts.note: a rim is an edge
and means together with, accompanied by

explanation.surface: An edge returns alongside a female lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses RIM to give MIR. Miranda is the heroine of Shakespeare's The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Miranda is the heroine of Shakespeare's The Tempest, Prospero's daughter.

clue.text: Check out of a colliery

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-works
a colliery is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Someone clocks out of a coal mine at the end of a shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check out' looks like one phrase meaning to leave; 'Check' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine is to inspect or check something closely.

clue.text: Forms or settles

explanation.surface: A writer drafts or calms down.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose is to form or make up, and composes oneself means calms or settles down.

clue.text: Set back one's vacation?

explanation.surface: A holiday is postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: To recess is to set something back into a wall, and a recess is a break or holiday, as Parliament's.
